title: Determining Agricultural Classification
summary: Decision tree for whether land qualifies for agricultural classification: qualifying use, primary use, prior production season, and January 1 compatibility.
disclaimer: This flow chart provides general information and may not apply in every situation. A thorough review of each property is still required.
router_description: Determining agricultural classification. Decision tree for whether land qualifies for agricultural classification under sec. 70.32(2)(a)4 based on qualifying use, primary use, production season. Tax 18.05.

nodes.question: Is the land's use one of the following qualifying agricultural uses?
criteria: Tilled land devoted to crop production (see WPAM 14-A-12 to 14-A-23)
Pastured land devoted to livestock production (see WPAM 14-A-23 to 14-A-29)
Growing short-rotation woody crops, including poplars and willows, using agronomic practices (see WPAM 14-15)
Enrollment in a qualifying government program or easement (see DOR's Tax 18 Conservation Programs publication)

nodes.question: Was the land devoted primarily to that agricultural use?
nodes.definition: Tax 18.05(4) defines land devoted primarily to agricultural use as land in an agricultural use for the production season of the prior year, and not in a use that is incompatible with agricultural use on January 1 of the assessment year.
criteria: See WPAM 14-8 to 14-20 for what 'devoted primarily to agricultural use' means, including what information to collect when a crop or pasture use is questionable as to primary use

authorities.note: definition of 'devoted primarily to agricultural use'

authorities.cite: Nudo Holdings LLC v. City of Kenosha, 2022 WI 17
authorities.note: agricultural activity alone is not enough; the activity must be the land's primary use; minor and isolated activities do not constitute a primary use

authorities.cite: Thoma v. Village of Slinger, 2018 WI 45
authorities.note: actual use controls whether land qualifies for agricultural classification

authorities.cite: Ogden Family Trust v. Town of Delafield, 2019 WI 23
authorities.note: business income (federal income tax Schedule F) cannot be considered when determining if land is devoted primarily to agricultural use

nodes.question: Was the land devoted primarily to that use during the prior production season?
nodes.guidance: Generally, a spring/April planting to a fall/October harvest represents a production season. See WI DATCP agricultural statistics for additional details.

nodes.question: Was the land compatible with agricultural use on the January 1 assessment date?
criteria: The land's condition is consistent with the production season
The land is compatible with the associated crop production, animal production, or program activity
The land contains no development of improvements

authorities.note: classification examples, including parcels with less than 40 acres; see the CQ for additional information

nodes.label: Qualifies for agricultural classification
nodes.action: Assessor classifies the land agricultural for the assessment year and distributes a Notice of Assessment if appropriate.

nodes.label: Does not qualify for agricultural classification
nodes.action: Land does not qualify for agricultural classification. The assessor classifies the land according to sec. 70.32, Wis. Stats., for the assessment year and distributes a Notice of Changed Assessment if appropriate.
